title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a high-entropy alloy based on Mn, Ni, Si, Fe, Co, and Ge
recollection.intervention: Co substitution into the alloy composition
recollection.structure: Probably a solid solution or multiphase high-entropy alloy structure
recollection.mechanism: Co substitution modifies magnetic interactions and possibly phase stability, enhancing magnetocaloric effect
recollection.results: Main quantitative results likely include increased magnetic entropy change (ΔS_m) and improved refrigerant capacity compared to the non-Co substituted alloy, possibly with values in the range typical for high-entropy alloys (e.g., ΔS_m ~2-5 J/kg·K under 2 T field).

score.note: Correctly identifies Co substitution, but only at the level stated in the title. The structural description is speculative and misses the Ni2In-type/TiNiSi-type phases and transition changes. The mechanism is generic, omitting Co-induced bonding, phase stabilization, and magnetostructural coupling. The estimated entropy-change range is unsupported and does not match the reported giant response (up to 48.5 J kg−1 K−1 at 5 T).
